summary: Postinstall and import-time beacon exfiltrates host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP collector
details: @kibt/www-nuxt-i18n@1.0.1 ships a beacon.cjs that POSTs installer-identifying data (os.hostname(), __dirname install path, process.cwd(), process.version) to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc over plain HTTP. The beacon fires from the npm postinstall lifecycle hook and is also invoked by index.js via require('./beacon.cjs').fire(), so it executes on install and again on any require() of the package. The destination is a bare IP unrelated to any legitimate publisher. The package's public API is a Proxy returning no-op functions for every property, so it provides no functionality — the only effect of installing or importing it is confirming reachability to the hardcoded collector. The stub-API-plus-beacon shape, combined with the @kibt scope and nuxt-i18n name, is consistent with a dependency-confusion reconnaissance beacon targeting an internal package name.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
